subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, make cron inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep cron control limited to per-job `toolsAllow` and delivery safeguards?
rationale: The choice defines a scheduled-run tool-execution boundary and a new public config contract, so automation should not choose the permanent security semantics or compatibility behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-specific policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against global, agent, group, sandbox, subagent, inherited, and per-job `toolsAllow` policy.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as covered by `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling cron and subagent semantics.

options.title: Keep current safeguards
options.body: Continue relying on per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery-mode safeguards, preserving today’s config surface while leaving this operator-wide deny request unsolved.

recommendation.title: Add cron-specific policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against global, agent, group, sandbox, subagent, inherited, and per-job `toolsAllow` policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest prior review and cron-runtime routing history for this exact policy decision.
